newsitem.title: USA: Compost gets N.J. plant expansion permit.
newsitem.headline: Compost gets N.J. plant expansion permit.

text.p: Compost America Holding Co Inc on Thursday said it has received a significantly upgraded permit and a solid waste license from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection.
Both authorizations pertain to the operation of a recycling and composting facility in Newark, N.J., by Compost America's wholly owned subsidiary, Newark Recycling and Composting Co Inc.
Upon completion of construction, it is anticipated that the Newark plant will generate about $25 million in annual revenue to Compost America, the company said.

The "Air Quality" construction permit and operating certificate is an upgrade of a permit issued earlier by the department. The upgrade allows Newark Recycling to process up to 1,200 wet tons per day of total waste materials, including a maximum of 600 wet tons of wastewater sludge, at the Newark plant.
The original permit allowed a total of 640 wet tons per day
The 'A901' license gives Compost America full clearance to operate all of its recycling and composting facilities located within the State of New Jersey, the company said.
